pr_title: Port some CoreRT Threading classes to Mono
pr_body:
Draft until I see how this behaves on CI.

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/44795

A few notes:

I've attempted to nullable annotate the relevant files but would appreciate someone else checking over my work, since the design does not really lend itself to that.

I can split the time-related parts of the System.Native addition off into a separate header if desired, but since they wouldn't be used elsewhere I just put the relevant includes in the C file.

This can fairly easily be moved to shared if desired, but I've put it in Mono only for now. Given there's a chance we might want to share it eventually after testing in Mono, I've left a CORERT define.

The `TARGET_UNIX` define usage isn't ideal, but given we care about the layout for that particular class it seemed like the easiest option. If it's a problem please let me know.
pr_comments: Splitting up into multiple PRs per feedback.

issue_context.title: Move System.Threading.Event/Mutex/Semaphore support to managed code
issue_context.body: These synchronization classes have little to do with the runtime and they can be implemented mostly in managed code as done in corert.
comments: Could they be rewritten into something else or use C# module initializers instead?

> WaitSubsystem makes use of EagerStaticClassConstruction.

It is because of the synchronization of static constructors depends on WaitSubsystem in CoreRT. I do not expect that you will have nor want to introduce this dependency in Mono.

It should be fine to just put use of this attribute under `#if CORERT` ifdef.

Tagging subscribers to 'size-reduction': @eerhardt, @SamMonoRT, @marek-safar, @tannergooding, @CoffeeFlux See info in area-owners.md if you want to be subscribed.

review_comments: I do not see anything Mono-specific in this file. Can it be in the shared partition and not have .Mono in name?

Have you done any changes to these files? For review, I would be useful to have separate commit (or even PR) that just copies the files over, so that it easy to review any changes you have done on top of it.

I have indeed made changes, mostly the annotations but also removing some CoreRT-specific invocations. Happy to go back and split the commit up, it was just annoying to do initially since I was fixing a host of build errors.

The most up to date version of these files is in https://github.com/dotnet/runtimelab/tree/feature/NativeAOT/src/coreclr/nativeaot/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Threading. Not sure whether you have copied them from there, or somewhere else.

>  I would be useful to have separate commit (or even PR)

Looks like we may be iterating on this a bit, so I would recommend to submit PR that just copies the needed files over, without any changes and without hooking it to the build. And then separate PR to hook it up to the build and make the necessary adjustments. It will make the review easier.

Can you add these files to the shared partition, and ifdef them out for CoreCLR in the build script for now?

We will want to switch CoreCLR to this eventually as well, and having it in the shared place will makes it easier. It is similar how the portable threadpool was done. It was enabled for Mono only, and later for CoreCLR too.
